statement: TVK won 108 of the 234 Assembly seats in 2026, short of the majority mark of 118.
C. Joseph Vijay was sworn in as Chief Minister on 10 May 2026 with nine ministers.
Vijay won both Perambur and Tiruchirappalli East and kept Perambur, vacating Tiruchirappalli East.
The government won the trust vote on 13 May 2026 by 144 votes to 22, with 5 MLAs neutral.
The DMK's 59 MLAs walked out of the 13 May trust vote.
In the trust vote TVK cast 105 votes, Congress 5, CPI(M), CPI, VCK and IUML 2 each, and an expelled AMMK MLA 1, alongside AIADMK rebels.
The VCK set conditions for its support, including a law against caste killings and opposition to delimitation.
Congress joined a Tamil Nadu government on 21 May 2026 for the first time since 1967.
Six AIADMK MLAs resigned their seats after the 2026 result.
Former AIADMK MLAs K. Maragatham Kumaravel (Madurantakam) and P. Sathyabama (Dharapuram) resigned on 25 May, joined TVK and won the 6 October 2026 by-polls as TVK candidates.
TVK's winning margin over the DMK in the 6 October Madurantakam by-poll is reported differently by outlets.
In the Dharapuram by-poll TVK's P. Sathyabama polled 66,841 votes to the DMK's 57,370, a margin of 9,471, with the AIADMK third.
Five Assembly seats remain vacant: Tiruchirappalli East, Perundurai, Ambasamudram, Viralimalai and Karur.
On 24 September 2026 the Madras High Court dismissed a PIL seeking a deposit from the six resigned AIADMK MLAs and a five-year disqualification.

On 13 October 2026 the Madras High Court upheld Speaker J.C.D. Prabhakar's acceptance of the six resignations and told him to decide AIADMK whip Krishnamurthy's disqualification petition within two months.
The Supreme Court dismissed the appeal against the High Court's ruling on the six resignations, as reported on 26 October 2026.
idly's calculation: two months from the 13 October order puts the Speaker's deadline on the disqualification petition at about 13 December 2026; the petition is still pending.
In his first speech as CM on 10 May 2026 Vijay asked for "some time" and said the treasury had been "completely emptied"; no report gives a fixed period.
MNM chief Kamal Haasan said on 17 May 2026 that Vijay should be given six months.
On 13 May 2026, the day of the trust vote, DMK's Udhayanidhi Stalin alleged horse-trading.
response: ThePrint's report of the charge carries no TVK reply; no court or agency finding has been reported.

statement: A South First survey of over 100 people on 8-9 November 2026, not a scientific poll, found 60.9% said the government failed expectations and 71.3% had little or no confidence.
The council of ministers reached 35 including the Chief Minister by 22 May 2026, the constitutional maximum of 15% of 234 seats.
The 35-member council has 31 TVK ministers, 2 Congress, 1 VCK and 1 IUML.
On 21 May 2026 23 more ministers were sworn in (21 TVK, 2 Congress), Finance moved from Sengottaiyan to first-time MLA N. Marie Wilson, and a new AI ministry was created.
idly's calculation: the Finance portfolio changed hands five days after it was first allotted (16 to 21 May 2026); no official reason was given.
No cabinet reshuffle or removal was found between 22 May and 10 November 2026.
idly could source prior ministerial experience for one of the 35 ministers, K.A. Sengottaiyan (MLA since 1977), and prior legislative experience for two, adding N. Anand (Puducherry MLA, 2006).
The TVK council has 8 Scheduled Caste ministers, 7 from the 21 May induction plus VCK's Vanni Arasu, a record for Tamil Nadu.
The TVK council has four women ministers.
The TVK council has two Brahmin ministers; HR&CE Minister S. Ramesh said no posts were given on caste consideration.
The DMK's first cabinet in 2021 had 34 members including the CM on day one, with 15 new faces, 3 SC ministers and 2 women.
The AIADMK's 2016 cabinet had 29 members at oath, with at most 2 SC ministers at any point in 2016-21.
The AIADMK government made three cabinet reshuffles by 4 November 2011 and dropped six ministers that day without official reasons.
The Centre approved a six-month extension for Chief Secretary M. Sai Kumar, from 1 September 2026 to 28 February 2027; he was installed by the Election Commission on 8 April 2026 and kept by TVK.
The debt the TVK government inherited for 2025-26 is put at different levels by the DMK's interim budget and the TVK white paper.

about Rs 10 lakh crore (TVK white paper, 16 Jun 2026)

The white paper put state-company (PSU) debt at Rs 3.18 lakh crore.
The 2025-26 debt-to-GSDP ratio differs between the white paper and the budget documents.
The TVK budget estimates debt at Rs 10,98,768 crore, 27.01% of GSDP, at the end of 2026-27.
The DMK's interim budget of 17 February 2026 had projected debt of Rs 10.71 lakh crore, 26.12% of GSDP, at the end of 2026-27.

Tamil Nadu's 2025-26 debt is the highest of any state, but the figure differs by source; a Union Rajya Sabha reply put it as the only state above Rs 10 lakh crore, ahead of Maharashtra (Rs 9.37 lakh crore) and Uttar Pradesh (Rs 8.84 lakh crore).

statement: idly's calculation: debt roughly doubled each five-year term, from Rs 2.23 lakh crore (2015-16) to Rs 4.80 lakh crore (2020-21), about 2.2 times, then to Rs 9.52 lakh crore (2025-26 RE), about 2 times.

Finance Minister N. Marie Wilson released a white paper on state finances on 16 June 2026.
The 2025-26 revenue deficit in the white paper does not match the figure in the TVK's own budget seven weeks later; the gap is Rs 9,105 crore and no report explains it.

The TVK budget puts the 2026-27 revenue deficit at Rs 55,775 crore, 1.4% of GSDP.
The TVK budget sets the 2026-27 fiscal deficit at Rs 1,21,819 crore, 3% of GSDP, the same ratio as the DMK interim budget's Rs 1.21 lakh crore.

The TVK budget put 2026-27 revenue receipts at Rs 3,50,027 crore, Rs 5,452 crore above the interim budget its white paper called overstated by about Rs 14,000 crore; a South First fact-check found the two documents not reconciled.
The 2026-27 budget puts the state's own tax revenue at Rs 2,26,740 crore.
Salaries, pensions and interest take Rs 2,14,728 crore, 61% of revenue receipts, against a 50% average for states.
RBI data shows interest took 20.8% of Tamil Nadu's revenue receipts in 2025-26, against 12.2% for all states, Kerala 20.9%, Karnataka 15.6%, Gujarat 12.4% and Maharashtra 11.5%.

statement: The 2026-27 budget provides for gross borrowing of Rs 1,73,445 crore.
The 2026-27 budget set Rs 812 crore for a wedding gold coin and saree, Rs 560 crore for a 1-gram gold ring for babies born in government hospitals, and Rs 110 crore for a goat scheme.
Economist K. Jothi Sivagnanam found Rs 18,141 crore of cuts in the budget, including Rs 2,577 crore of capital spending, offsetting Rs 18,386 crore of new transfers.
The 2026-27 budget adds a privilege fee on liquor makers of up to Rs 1,000 crore a year and budgets own tax revenue up 10%.
The government expects about Rs 16,000 crore a year in extra revenue from tax reforms and a liquor privilege fee but has not explained the method.
Former finance minister Thangam Thennarasu called the white paper an "empty paper" repackaging budget data; idly's claim check rates that mostly true.
After the 5 August budget Edappadi K. Palaniswami called it "zero", citing the unmet Rs 2,500 promise; the government said no existing welfare scheme had been cut.
idly's claim check rates Vijay's 10 May claim that the DMK left Rs 10 lakh crore of debt mostly true, though about Rs 4.8 lakh crore predates 2021.
idly's claim check rates Vijay's claim that the DMK "emptied the treasury" unverifiable, because no cash-balance figure has been published.
idly's claim check rates Stalin's 10 May claim that debt was within the permitted limit misleading, as the DMK's own figures show a 2025-26 fiscal deficit of 3.48%, above the 3% norm.
Tamil Nadu's gross GST fell year on year every month from May to September 2026 (worst May, -15.1%) and rose 3% in October against 22.9% nationally.
State officials say the post-settlement GST share rose 15% from April to October 2026 and 8% in October.
TASMAC raised the printed price of liquor by Rs 10 a bottle from 1 November 2026, five weeks after Minister K. Vignesh said there would be no retail price rise in the near future.
On 9 August 2021 the DMK's Finance Minister P. Thiaga Rajan released a white paper calling the AIADMK's finances "unsustainable" and projecting debt of about Rs 5.7 lakh crore by March 2022.
The AIADMK's R.B. Udhayakumar asked why the 2021 white paper was needed and noted the DMK's Rs 1,000 a month for women was unpaid.
The 2021 white paper put debt at 24.98% of GSDP when the DMK took office.
The debt the DMK inherited in 2021 differs by source.

statement: The TVK's Medium Term Fiscal Plan sets the fiscal deficit at 3.00% of GSDP in 2026-27, 2.87% in 2027-28 and 2.80% in 2028-29.
The plan projects revenue deficits of Rs 55,775 crore (2026-27), Rs 53,933 crore (2027-28) and Rs 51,058 crore (2028-29).
The plan targets debt of 27.01% of GSDP in 2026-27, 26.57% in 2027-28 and 26.10% in 2028-29.
Planned interest rises to Rs 89,698 crore in 2027-28 and Rs 1,02,256 crore in 2028-29; the 2026-27 figure differs by source.
idly's calculation: the plan assumes nominal GSDP grows 14% a year (Rs 40,67,312 crore in 2026-27 to Rs 52,85,879 crore in 2028-29), and interest also grows 14% a year.
idly's calculation: with a 3% deficit and 27% debt, the debt ratio holds at about 12.5% nominal growth, falls about 0.3 points a year at 14%, and rises about 0.3 points a year at 11%.
idly's calculation: the TVK's 2028-29 debt target of 26.10% is almost the 26.12% the DMK set for 2026-27.
Under the 16th Finance Commission (2026-27 to 2030-31) Tamil Nadu's share of central taxes moves from 4.079% to 4.097%.

The 16th Finance Commission caps the fiscal deficit at 3% of GSDP each year, bars carrying forward unused borrowing room, ends revenue-deficit grants and asks states to bring off-budget borrowing onto their books.
idly's calculation: if all Rs 3.18 lakh crore of PSU debt moved onto the budget, the reported debt ratio would jump by about 7.8 points of GSDP in one step.
A revenue committee chaired by Montek Singh Ahluwalia, set up in July 2026, has not reported and has no stated deadline.
The 2026-27 budget set aside Rs 14,414 crore for the Rs 1,000 women's aid scheme and nothing for the promised rise to Rs 2,500.
The Hindu, as cited by South First, put the Rs 2,500 scheme at about Rs 39,000 crore a year for 1.3 crore women.

idly's calculation: on the Rs 39,000 crore estimate the Rs 2,500 adds about Rs 24,600 crore a year, which with no other change would lift the 2027-28 fiscal deficit from 2.87% to about 3.4%, or about 3.05% even if the Rs 16,000 crore revenue target were met.
idly's calculation: if nominal growth stays at 12-14% and the deficit is held at 3%, debt would sit at about 26.5-27.5% of GSDP by November 2027.
idly's calculation: if nominal growth slows to about 11%, debt would rise to roughly 27.6-27.7% of GSDP by 2028-29 instead of falling to 26.1%.

idly's calculation: past realisation rates applied to the Rs 67,452 crore conclave give about Rs 5,700 crore at 8.5%, Rs 18,200 crore at 27% and Rs 37,100 crore at 55%; these rates took 2.5 to 6 years.
The AIADMK's GIM 2015 in September 2015 signed 98 MoUs worth about Rs 2.42 lakh crore.
The DMK said in 2021 that 64 of GIM 2015's 98 projects were taken up, but the realised amount differs by source; the AIADMK's own 2017 figure was 62 MoUs implemented.
The AIADMK's GIM 2019 signed 304 MoUs; the committed value differs by source.
The DMK said in 2021 that GIM 2019 realised Rs 80,512 crore (about 26-27%), with 150-151 of 304 projects taken up.
DMK minister T.R.B. Rajaa said in 2024 that Edappadi K. Palaniswami's 2019 foreign tours produced 27 MoUs worth Rs 5,087 crore, of which Rs 434 crore (8.53%) was realised.
DMK ministers gave different realised totals for the AIADMK's GIM 2015 and 2019 combined.
alt_values: about Rs 1.46 lakh crore (idly's calculation from Thennarasu's 2021 figures)

statement: The DMK's GIM 2024 signed 631 MoUs worth Rs 6.64 lakh crore; Minister T.R.B. Rajaa said in 2025 that nearly 80% had been grounded.
The DMK government said its 1,179 MoUs from May 2021 to February 2026 were worth Rs 12.37 lakh crore, with 73.53% at an "advanced stage" and 35.11% "in operation", giving no realised-rupee figure.

Definitions of MoU "conversion" differ: the DMK's 2021 statement on AIADMK meets counted commercial production, while its own record counted MoUs at ground-breaking or advanced stage; no independent audit exists.
On 4 June 2026 the TVK government signed an MoU with L&T for Rs 18,600 crore and about 8,200 jobs.
The TVK's Vettri Tamil Nadu conclave on 13 August 2026, closed to the media, produced 97 company MoUs and 7 institutional agreements; the reported value differs.
Projected jobs from the 13 August conclave differ by source.

idly's calculation: the government's claim of Rs 1,02,514 crore investment "attracted" in 100 days equals Rs 35,062 crore from seven pre-conclave MoUs plus the conclave's Rs 67,452 crore, so it is MoU commitments, not money invested.

Former industries minister T.R.B. Rajaa said about 70 of the 97 conclave MoUs were expansions or leads from the DMK period, worth about 75% of the value, giving no method; Minister S. Keerthana said the conclave mixed new investors and expansions without giving a split.
The government put Vijay's September 2026 London trip at Rs 15,300 crore; named deals add to Rs 12,300 crore, led by Samvardhana Motherson's Rs 11,000 crore, with Rs 3,000 crore not itemised.

In November 2026 three Korean suppliers to Hyundai and Kia chose Anantapur in Andhra Pradesh for Rs 1,614 crore of projects and 1,418 jobs; Stalin said the state was in "reverse gear" and the Industries Department called that framing a distortion, saying suppliers follow carmakers.
Kia's car plant of about US$1.1 billion went to Andhra Pradesh in 2017 under the AIADMK; the state government said Kia's policy barred a unit where Hyundai operates.
First Solar's 3.3 GW plant at Tirunelveli, announced under the DMK, has operated since January 2024.
VinFast's EV plant at Thoothukudi (US$500 million phase 1) has operated since 4 August 2025.
The Rs 9,000 crore Tata Motors/JLR plant at Ranipet has operated since 9 February 2026.
Ola's Krishnagiri cell gigafactory, committed at 20 GWh, was scaled back to 5 GWh until FY29 and received a Union notice for a missed milestone.
Chennai Metro Phase II (Rs 63,246 crore) opened its first 14.6 km stretch on 11 October 2026; one stretch had been due in December 2025.

The Perur desalination plant is under construction, now due "by 2027" instead of before December 2026; its cost moved from Rs 4,276 crore (2023) to Rs 5,814.57 crore (2026 report) without explanation.
The Hosur airport (about Rs 19,000 crore) is stalled after the Defence Ministry refused airspace clearance.
The Rs 985.96 crore Kulasekarapattinam spaceport is under construction, with commissioning targeted for 2026-27.

The TVK government cancelled the DMK's Parandur airport (about Rs 27,400 crore) in the Assembly on 24 August 2026, citing farmland and water bodies; about 1,700 acres of private land had already been bought.
The Rs 2,100 crore ECR elevated corridor is reported stalled without formal cancellation, and a Rs 261 crore sports city order and a Rs 310 crore flyover tender were cancelled.
In 2011 the AIADMK turned the DMK-built Secretariat complex into a hospital and set up an inquiry into its construction.
Vijay signed three files on 10 May 2026: 200 free power units per two-month bill, a women's safety force (Singappen) and an Anti-Narcotics Task Force.
From 10 May 2026 homes using up to 500 units get 200 free units per two-month bill (up from 100), covering about 1.46 crore consumers at Rs 1,730 crore a year extra subsidy.
idly's calculation: the free-power change saves about Rs 99 a month per eligible home on average (Rs 1,730 crore / 1.46 crore / 12).
The DMK's Kalaignar Magalir Urimai Thogai of Rs 1,000 a month continues for about 1.31 crore women, renamed Magalir Urimai Thittam, with Rs 14,414 crore budgeted and the list being re-surveyed.
On the Rs 2,500, Minister K. Jegadeshwari said on 5 July there was "no ambiguity" and on 6 July "very soon", and the Finance Secretary said on 5 August it would come within a year.
Free bus travel for women (DMK's Vidiyal Payanam) was widened to express, deluxe and mofussil buses and renamed Vettri Payanam from 2 October 2026, at about Rs 6,000 crore a year.
A 2022 State Planning Commission survey of 1,275 women found the DMK-era free bus scheme saved women about Rs 888 a month on average.

sources.outlet: Tamil Nadu State Planning Commission study

statement: Announced on 24 August 2026, Annapoorani Super Six repays the price of three LPG cylinders a year to families earning up to Rs 2.5 lakh, about 1.30 crore families, from Pongal (January 2027), at about Rs 4,000 crore; none was paid by 10 November.
idly's calculation: the LPG scheme is worth about Rs 256 a month per eligible family once paid (Rs 4,000 crore / 1.30 crore / 12).
From 16 October 2026 fine rice is sold at Rs 30 a kg (up to 5 kg) at about 250 co-operative outlets; idly's calculation puts the saving at Rs 225-275 per 5 kg against open-market rice at Rs 75-85.
The milk procurement price was raised from Rs 38 to Rs 44 a litre for about 3.16 lakh dairy farmers.
Around 28 October 2026 Aavin raised ghee from Rs 700 to Rs 780 a litre, 500 ml curd from Rs 35 to Rs 40 and 500 g butter from Rs 275 to Rs 320; retail milk was unchanged to 10 November.
The first crop-loan waiver announcement on 25 May 2026 was capped at Rs 50,000; Edappadi K. Palaniswami called it a "betrayal".
On 16 June 2026 the waiver limit was raised to Rs 75,000 for loans taken 1 May 2025 to 28 February 2026, for about 14.43 lakh farmers at Rs 5,932.23 crore.

A Co-operation Department order of 6 November 2026 drops the tiers and waives up to Rs 75,000 for every eligible borrower with loans from 1 May 2025 to 31 March 2026: 13,24,882 farmers, Rs 9,062.83 crore in all.
idly's calculation: the crop-loan waiver averages about Rs 68,400 per borrower (Rs 9,062.83 crore / 13.25 lakh).
The DMK announced a co-operative jewel-loan waiver for up to five sovereigns on 13 September 2021, about four months after taking office, at an estimated Rs 6,000 crore; it was later discontinued.

Sugarcane is priced at Rs 4,000 a tonne with the incentive paid by bank transfer from Deepavali, Rs 603.34 crore for the 2025-26 season; idly's calculation puts it at about Rs 67,000 per grower for about 90,000 growers.
Paddy procurement is Rs 2,750 a quintal for fine and Rs 2,600 for common varieties from 1 September 2026.

The CM's Breakfast Scheme was renamed the Perunthalaivar Kamarajar Breakfast Scheme on 15 July 2026 and extended to Classes 6-8 from 17 September for about 15.14 lakh more pupils (Rs 343.55 crore for the extension; Rs 710 crore in all).

Several DMK schemes were renamed with a "Vetri" prefix, including Naan Mudhalvan (now Vetri Skill Training, Rs 150 crore), Ungal Kaiyil Ulagam laptops (Vetri Laptop, Rs 2,000 crore) and Kalaignar Kanavu Illam (Vetri Veedu, Rs 3,500 crore, unit cost Rs 3.1 lakh to Rs 5 lakh).
No DMK welfare scheme was found to have been dropped; the Finance Secretary said none was discontinued, while Edappadi K. Palaniswami said the government had put stickers on existing schemes.
In 2021 the DMK kept AIADMK schemes under their names, including Amma Canteens, and handed out schoolbags carrying Palaniswami's picture rather than spend over Rs 13 crore replacing them.

The Thaimaaman Thanga Mothiram scheme gives a 1-gram gold ring to babies born in government hospitals from 22 June 2026; it launched on 28 September and Udhayanidhi Stalin says the promise covered all children.

The Annan Seer scheme of 8 g gold and a silk saree for brides was ordered on 5 October 2026 with an income limit of Rs 2.5 lakh (promise Rs 5 lakh) and Rs 812 crore; the tender for 60,000 gold coins closes on 8 December and no coins had been given by 10 November.
idly's calculation: of 16 TVK scorecard rows on 10 November 2026, 2 were delivered, 5 partly, 3 started, 4 not started and 2 could not be verified.
On 28 September 2026 Leader of the Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin listed the LPG, unemployment-aid and farm-loan promises as unfulfilled.
The government's line, as Finance Minister Marie Wilson was reported to say, is that promises will be phased over one, three and five years.
TVK released its manifesto on 16 April 2026 with Rs 2,500 a month for women heads of family, free LPG cylinders and gold for brides as headline items.

Stalin signed five files on 7 May 2021: Rs 4,000 COVID relief per rice card, Aavin milk Rs 3 a litre cheaper, free town-bus travel for women, a petitions department with a 100-day target, and COVID treatment in private hospitals under the CM's insurance.

Jayalalithaa signed seven files on 16 May 2011 as PTI counted them, including 20 kg free rice a month, 4 g gold for brides' thali, marriage aid of Rs 25,000-50,000 and old-age pension raised from Rs 500 to Rs 1,000.

Jayalalithaa signed five files on 23 May 2016, including a co-operative farm loan waiver for small and marginal farmers (est. Rs 5,780 crore), 100 free power units (est. Rs 1,607 crore), gold for brides raised to 8 g and 500 TASMAC shops shut.
The DMK's promised Rs 1,000 a month for women heads of family launched on 15 September 2023, about 28 months after it took office, with eligibility rules rather than for every head of family.

The DMK's NEET exemption Bill passed the Assembly on 13 September 2021 with AIADMK, PMK and VCK support while the BJP walked out; five years later NEET still applies and the TVK CM was still seeking exemption in November 2026.
Tamil Nadu's infant mortality rate fell from 22 per 1,000 live births in 2011 to 12 in 2023, against 25 for India; the 2019 value differs by source.
Tamil Nadu's maternal mortality ratio fell from 97 per lakh live births in 2007-09 to 35 in 2021-23, second lowest in India, against 88 nationally.
Stunted children under five in Tamil Nadu fell from 27.1% in NFHS-4 (2015-16) to 25.0% in NFHS-5 (2019-21).
Wasted children under five fell from 19.7% (NFHS-4, 2015-16) to 14.6% (NFHS-5, 2019-21).
Anaemic women aged 15-49 fell from 55.0% (NFHS-4, 2015-16) to 53.4% (NFHS-5, 2019-21).
Anaemic children aged 6-59 months rose from 50.7% (NFHS-4, 2015-16) to 57.4% (NFHS-5, 2019-21).
Births in an institution rose from 98.9% (NFHS-4, 2015-16) to 99.6% (NFHS-5, 2019-21).
The share of Tamil Nadu's people in multidimensional poverty fell from 36.54% in 2005-06 to 2.20% in 2019-21 and a projected 1.43% in 2022-23, against India's 11.28%.

AAP won 92 of 117 Punjab seats in March 2022, lost the Sangrur Lok Sabha by-poll by 5,822 votes three months later, and won 3 of 13 Lok Sabha seats in June 2024.
YSRCP won 151 of 175 Andhra Pradesh seats in May 2019, all 11 municipal corporations in March 2021, and then 4 of 25 Lok Sabha and 11 of 175 Assembly seats in 2024.

statement: Andhra Pradesh Deputy CM Pawan Kalyan said on 25 May 2026, in an indirect reference to Vijay, "it even makes me feel envious", after telling workers on 17 May not to compare him with Vijay.

Karnataka CM D.K. Shivakumar said on 18 June 2026 that Mekedatu "will help Tamil Nadu more than Karnataka" and he was ready to talk to Vijay; TN Agriculture Minister R. Vinoth said on 24 July Tamil Nadu would "never allow" it.

After the TN budget sought a higher Mullaperiyar level, Kerala Water Resources Minister Mons Joseph said on 5 August 2026 "we will not allow the water level" to be raised, and Kerala CM V.D. Satheesan said a CM-level meeting was being considered.
Telangana CM A. Revanth Reddy told Vijay on 10 May 2026: "I strongly believe that you will deliver welfare for the poor".
Rahul Gandhi said on 10 May 2026 "Tamil Nadu has chosen. A new generation. A new voice." and on 22 June pledged to stand with Vijay on the rights of Tamil people.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi, opening projects worth about Rs 13,000 crore in Chennai on 11 October 2026, said "Together with CM Vijay, we are taking forward the development of the state."

On 13 October 2025, on TVK's petition, the Supreme Court moved the probe into the 27 September 2025 Karur crowd crush, in which 41 people died, to the CBI under a committee led by former judge Ajay Rastogi; the cause is for the investigation to establish.
On 2 December 2025 the then DMK government asked the Supreme Court to cancel the CBI probe and restore the police team; no report shows the TVK government withdrawing, pressing or changing that plea.
On 7 July 2026 the Supreme Court declined a DMK plea to stop the CM speaking about the Karur case, noting he is not an accused in the FIRs; the DMK withdrew.
The CBI filed a first inquiry report in October 2025 and a charge sheet was expected by end-February 2026, but none had been reported as of 10 November 2026.

Former DMK School Education Minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi was arrested on 26 October 2026 in a Prevention of Corruption Act case alleging money was collected from private schools as a "party fund"; a special court refused bail on 10 November.
response: He called the September searches politically motivated and said nothing illegal was found; his lawyers argued a collective decision was being painted as corruption and that the Governor's sanction was not obtained; Stalin called it "political vendetta". No charge sheet has been reported.

statement: After the 6 Oct 2026 by-polls TVK has 109 or 110 MLAs (sources differ), against a majority mark of 118 in the 234-seat Assembly; five seats are vacant.
In the 13 May 2026 trust vote (144 for, 22 against, 5 neutral), the number of AIADMK MLAs who backed the government is reported as 25, 24 or 22 (sources differ).
